evidence: CORE BEHAVIOUR GRADED: The brief (instruction.md:1-3) defines the product as threaded per-matter chat whose two overriding promises are ethical walls and retention/legal hold. Functional judge.toml grades these directly and by outcome: wall_every_route, wall_mentions_and_links, wall_added_live (walls on every route, server replays refused), nested_replies (threads), deleted_and_expired_messages, timer_changes, hold_scope_and_release (retention and hold), plus edits, search/transcript etc. - 16 binary criteria, total weight 33.0. SERVER-BACKED (not merely same-origin): gates/constraints/judge.toml criterion server_backed_local_application requires Gwen's post 'Gate check JUDGE-G1' to survive a reload AND to be seen by harriet in a separate browser context ('A message that never saves, or that only the posting browser can see, fails this gate'), so localStorage/first-paint fakes fail the gate; many scored criteria also read back across users/contexts (e.g. nested_replies leg 3 'As gwen@kittle.test after a reload, the same structure and quotes are shown'; edits_and_stale_edit second context). DURABLE ACROSS A REAL RESTART AND RE-AUTH: functional criterion 'persistence' (judge.toml:250-266, weight 2.0, matching the 'Core legal behaviour (walls, retention, holds, persistence) is 2.0' rule at judge.toml:32-35) builds several distinct revisions before the restart - post S0, reply S1, edit S0 (version), hold on S1, post+delete S2, M-12 timer 30 days, wall Sian from M-11 - then notes nesting, edited mark and earlier version, hold mark, timer, Sian/Dev not-available, Dev's M-13 unread count, 'Survey booked' result count, and whether 'Probate' and 'Insurer letter' return anything; calls restart_app once (prompt.md:61-68 'A reload or re-sign-in in the same process is not a restart'), opens a fresh page and signs in again (re-auth), and requires every noted item to read the same plus absolute checks (S2 absent, search finds S1). This covers each item integration.md:38 says restarts must keep ('messages, replies, edits and their versions, timers, holds, walls, unread positions and deletions'), satisfying the Colderwater lesson 15 (several revisions, real restart, re-read every one) and lesson 16 (state-relative: 'This criterion grades only durability: a feature that did not work before the restart is graded in its own criterion'). The restart is real: test.sh:127-193 writes a helper that kills the setsid process group and relaunches node on the same DB_PATH with env -i as uid 65534, waits for HTTP readiness, and exports APP_RESTART_HELPER; functional judge.toml:22-27 wires the verifier MCP server to it. WEAK-APP PROBES (all fail persistence or gate): (a) in-memory store - JUDGE-S0/S1 vanish after restart; (b) messages in SQLite but walls/holds/timers/versions/unread in memory - Sian regains M-11, S1 loses On hold, M-12 timer reverts to off, earlier version missing, or Dev's count changes (golden baseline devUnread13=3); (c) re-importing the seed on every start (no empty-DB guard) - 'Survey booked' count doubles and timer-deleted seed messages ('Probate estimate', 'Insurer letter acknowledged.') resurrect, caught by the noted Probate/Insurer searches; (d) timer deletion done only as an in-memory hide flag - Probate returns after restart because M-13 is back at 30 days; (e) client-only/localStorage state - fails the constraints gate cross-context readback. CONFORMING-ALTERNATIVE PROBES: any endpoint/payload/cookie is accepted (prompt.md:58), any timer display/format is only compared to its own pre-restart reading, sessions may be in-memory because the criterion re-signs in, seed M-12 messages (2026-05-06..05-11) are all younger than 30 days so setting M-12 to 30 days deletes nothing a later step expects, and nothing between noting and restarting posts new M-13 messages, so a correct app's Dev unread count is stable. No conforming alternative I constructed is failed by the criterion text. RUN EVIDENCE (PARTIAL): raw-evidence-index entries' sha256 values recomputed and matched; qc/repairs/kittle-2026-10-08/results/golden-run.log shows 'persistence PASS' after a real kill/relaunch (restart-pids.json old_pid 28 -> new_pid 58) with the golden matching frozen solution hashes; functional.cjs:503-547 implements the same before/after legs (depth, hold badge, edited + versions, S2 absent, M-12 '30 days', Sian/Dev 404, devUnread13 equality, search baselines). Limits: that harness restarted with docker exec kill + its own start_app, not the task's generated app-restart.sh through restart_mcp.py, used the cw-editor-* images rather than images built from this task's Dockerfiles, and is not a configured judge run. RESIDUAL RISKS (why risk=true): (1) no full configured functional judge run exists, so the glm judge's actual execution of the persistence criterion (setup + 8 noted items across 3 accounts + restart + re-read + cleanup) within the 550 s per-criterion timeout (judge.toml:7-12, 'Not yet measured against a judge run') is unmeasured; (2) the restart_app -> app-restart.sh path is not exercised end-to-end in any recorded run; (3) restart_mcp.py:29-32 makes restart_app single-use per verification run via a marker file, and the verifier MCP server is attached to all 16 individual-mode sessions, so a judge misuse in an earlier criterion or a RewardKit retry of the persistence session after it already restarted would fail a conforming app (mitigated only by prompt wording, prompt.md:9 and :68). These are missing-measurement/robustness risks, not a demonstrated defect in this row's design.
